title: Console degraded-mode: minimal cost + tracing surface with staged fallbacks and acceptance criteria
creator: Linnea Chen
description:
Summary: Cut scope to ship a minimal Console surface that provides basic cost visibility and a lightweight tracing entry while guaranteeing predictable latency and low telemetry costs. This ticket defines the reduced scope, the staged fallback UX (degraded-mode), acceptance criteria, and follow-up/backfill work.

Background: The full Observability PRD included per-route cost breakdowns, continuous trace capture, and a heatmap of token-level cost. Engineering capacity and telemetry cost projections force a smaller initial surface. We will ship a compact feature set that retains signal for most users while deferring expensive instrumentation.

Primary goals: provide enough actionability for platform and app teams to identify top cost drivers and detect latency regressions without incurring high trace ingestion or storage costs. Enable a clear rollback and upgrade path for customers that need full fidelity later.

Scope removed for MVP:
- Remove continuous span capture for all requests (no full traces in initial launch).
- Remove route-level token-by-token cost waterfall; provide aggregate cost per model + top-3 routes sampling instead.
- Remove interactive cost heatmap visualization; support CSV export of sampled cost events.
- Defer per-token latency histograms and percentile breakdown beyond p50/p95.

Included in MVP (reduced surface):
- Quickcard: Total cost (7d, 30d) by model with delta and top-3 contributing routes (sampled API keys).
- Lightweight trace entry: one sampled trace per route per minute, linked to a plaintext event view (no span graph).
- Alerting hooks: simple SLO breach trigger and a link to degrade-mode diagnostics page.
- Degraded-mode UI: explicit banner explaining sampling + link to enable full capture in Dedicated/Private plans.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before marking Done):
- UI: Quickcard renders for orgs with activity; values match backend aggregates within 2% for total cost sample window.
- Sampling: Trace and route samples follow sampling policy (1/min per route by default) and sampling rate is configurable via feature flag.
- Backend: Cost aggregation pipeline produces model-level totals and top-3 sampled routes within 30s of event ingestion for 95% of cases.
- Performance: New endpoints add <15ms p50 and <35ms p95 to API-side join logic under normal load.
- Telemetry budget: Estimated telemetry cost for a medium customer (10k rps) must be <= 30% of full-PRD estimate; infra owners to sign off.
- Rollout: Feature gate enabled for internal-beta and 10 pilot customers with automated rollback if error rate increases >0.5% above baseline.
- Docs/UX: Console banner copy and degraded-mode FAQ pages created and approved by Design.
- Tests: End-to-end smoke tests for sampling, card rendering, and CSV export exist in QA harness and pass in CI.

Design tradeoffs and rationale:
- Why sampling not full traces: continuous tracing would increase ingestion costs and storage by an order of magnitude; sampling retains signal to detect regressions while keeping costs predictable.
- Why aggregate cost by model first: model-level economics is the highest-leverage metric for platform teams and matches our OLAs around model variant fallbacks.
- UX clarity: degrade-mode is explicit to avoid confusing customers who might expect full fidelity; links direct to upgrade paths.

Work items (implementation-ready):
1) Backend: sampling service + model-aggregate pipeline (ENG-59310 - engineering epic).
2) API: new compact endpoints: /cost/summary and /traces/sample (paginated plaintext) with feature flag.
3) Frontend: quickcard component, degraded-mode banner, CSV export flow.
4) Docs: degraded-mode FAQ, rollout instructions, observability playbook.
5) Telemetry estimate and infra signoff.

Follow-ups (post-MVP/backfill):
- Implement optional full-trace capture for Dedicated customers with retention controls.
- Add per-route waterfall and heatmap once sampling cost targets are met.
- Expand latency percentile granularity and token-level cost attribution.

Success metrics (30 days after rollout):
- Adoption: 25% of orgs with >1k monthly tokens view the quickcard at least once.
- Signal quality: teams opened 10 incidents that were diagnosable using sampled traces or quickcard insights.
- Cost: telemetry spend measured in production stays within projected budget.

Notes about compatibility: This reduced surface preserves existing API contracts for higher-level endpoints where possible; where contracts change we provide 2 weeks of deprecation warnings and a compatibility shim in the SDK.

acceptance_criteria: Quickcard shows 7d and 30d model totals and top-3 sampled routes with <=2% aggregate error
Sampling policy enforced: <=1 sample/min per route by default and configurable via feature flag
Backend aggregates visible within 30s for 95% of events
API performance impact: <15ms p50 and <35ms p95 on join endpoints
Telemetry budget signed off by infra and finance
Degraded-mode UI copy approved by Design and verified in staging
End-to-end QA smoke tests present and green in CI
Rollout gate: internal-beta + 10 pilots with rollback rules defined
decisions: Ship sampling-first tracing surface to control telemetry costs
Expose aggregate model cost as primary signal; defer per-route waterfall
Offer full-fidelity tracing as paid/dedicated feature rather than default
